method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the person who suffered harm and claims damages, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one small module (built-in date functions, no daydate), the s 5 reach and shared dictionary terms in a second, then three rule modules (liability; damages; institutional child abuse), each exported question calling a rule defined beside it, and a worked-case file for each; one regulative rule (s 33H(7)(a)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Civil Liability Act 2003 (Qld), act-2003-016, the version in force from 2024-07-01 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2003-016.txt (text sha256 2c8cbf78ced66ee1e759834912ef22a501cf77e7ccc5b0ffe94711551f766333 per its meta.json); with the Civil Liability Indexation Notice 2026 (sl-2026-0090, in force from 2026-07-01, text sha256 e563cdce7c8830c5559b00164e43d97c6baaf96c8d2e909368eba1337564bdc4) and the Civil Liability Regulation 2025 (sl-2025-0109, in force from 2025-09-01, text sha256 9700b12edc89c07c3a4f0d3600774200b610d50271197394e4ccf7f0d5746379), sch 1 and sch 2 ss 4, 14, deposited under their own subjects in subjects/au/qld/; all converted from the Queensland Legislation HTML view

seat: the person who suffered harm and claims damages for it: the injured person (or, for a death, the dependants or estate), the person harmed in property or economic loss, and the person abused as a child who claims against an institution (claq-common.l4, claq-liability.l4, claq-damages.l4, claq-abuse.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run <file> for each of the eight .l4 files, from this folder, at most two at a time
checks.result: 258 assertions written, 258 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the texts.

scope: Chapter 2 and chapter 3 as a claimant meets them, chapter 4 parts 1, 1A and 2, and the numbers the Indexation Notice 2026 and the Regulation 2025 set. In: ss 4(1), 5 (reach); s 9; ss 13-16; ss 17-19; ss 20-22; ss 25-27 with Regulation s 4, sch 1; ch 2 pt 2 ss 28, 29, 31, 32(1), 32D-32G; ch 2 pt 2A ss 33A-33I, 33J-33MA, 86 (33O, 33P as asked facts); ss 34-37; ss 38-44; s 45; ss 47-49 (s 24 in the answers); ss 49A, 49B; ch 3 ss 50-56, 58-62, 64, 66, 85 with Notice ss 3-5 and Regulation sch 2 ss 4, 14; ss 68-72D; s 73. Out: ss 1-3, 6, 7, 8, 74, 75 and chapter 5 except ss 85, 86 (machinery and transition); s 4(2)-(6) (the commencement and assent days are not in the deposited text); ss 10-12, 23, 35, 46 (principles for the court, no yes/no answer for the claimant; glossed in descriptions); ss 32(2)-(6), 32A-32C, 32H, 32I, 33 (between wrongdoers and the court); ss 33N, 33Q (machinery); ss 55(1)-(3), 57 (the court's method; the present value is asked); ss 59C, 59D (glossed; s 59D is the recipient's seat); ss 63, 65, 67 (court powers and costs); Regulation sch 3-5 (the ISV ranges and the psychiatric rating scale: the court's assessment, the ISV is asked). Reasons in NOTES.md.
